name: The Real Daughter Comes Home
blurb: Switched at birth, the real daughter comes home, and her sweet new sister plans her fall
title: The Real Daughter Comes Home: Short Drama Script (Ep 1)
description: A free 2.5-minute vertical family short drama script for 4 actors. A daughter switched at birth comes home, and her sister frames her. Free to film.
h1: The Real Daughter Comes Home: a 2.5-Minute Family Short Drama Script, Episode 1
logline: Twenty-two years after a hospital mix-up, May arrives at the rich family who lost her, carrying one plastic bag. Claire, the daughter they raised, greets her with a hug and a whispered threat, and by dinner a family heirloom is in May's bag.
setting: A front door, a dining table and a hallway. Props: a plastic bag of clothes, a pearl necklace (costume jewellery), plates and glasses, a phone.

roles.name: May
roles.note: 22, the real daughter, raised by a stallholder; quiet, observant, cannot be pushed around.

roles.name: Claire
roles.note: 22, the raised daughter; charming in public, ruthless in private.

roles.name: Helen
roles.note: 50s, the mother; loving, guilty, wants everyone to be happy.

roles.name: Arthur
roles.note: 50s, the father; kind, awkward, avoids conflict. Can be played as an uncle or a family friend.

script.scene: EXT. FRONT DOOR OF A LARGE HOUSE – DAY

script.action: MAY, twenty-two, in a worn denim jacket, holds a plastic bag of clothes. The door opens. CLAIRE, twenty-two, in a silk dress and pearls, smiles like a magazine cover.

script.say: You must be the real one. Welcome home, sister.

script.action: She pulls May into a hug, and whispers in her ear.

script.say: Nothing in this house is yours. Remember that.

script.action: She lets go, beaming. HELEN, fifties, and ARTHUR, fifties, hurry to the door.

script.say: May. Twenty-two years. Let me look at you.
Come in, come in. Claire has been so excited.
I made up the guest room myself.

script.action: A long table. May sits stiffly. Claire passes her the salt before she asks for it.

script.say: Claire tells us you worked in a little shop, May?
A jewellery repair stall. Under a bridge. My dad ran it until he got sick. I fixed watches.
That's so brave. I could never work with my hands.
You'll never have to work like that again, love.

script.action: Claire touches her bare throat and gasps.

script.say: Mum. My grandmother's necklace. I took it off before dinner. It was on my dresser.
Are you sure?
Nobody else has been upstairs today. Except...

script.action: Silence. Arthur picks up May's plastic bag from beside her chair, embarrassed, and looks inside. He lifts out a pearl necklace.

script.say: May?
It's all right. She grew up with nothing. I'd want things too.
May I see it?

script.action: She takes the necklace. Turns a pearl in the light. Taps it against her front tooth.

script.say: This is glass. Real pearls feel gritty on your teeth. These are smooth. And the clasp is cheap metal. It's already going green.
That's not possible. That necklace has been in the family for sixty years.
The real one was. This copy is about three months old.
So where's the real one, Claire? And why did your copy end up in my bag?

script.action: Every face turns to Claire. Her lip trembles. Tears come instantly.

script.say: You think I'd steal from my own mother?
I think you'd frame your new sister on her first night. That's quicker.

script.action: Helen stares at the necklace. Arthur stares at Claire. Claire runs from the room.
Claire, eyes dry now, makes a phone call in a whisper.

script.say: She knows about the necklace. She's not stupid like you promised.

script.action: She glances down the hallway at May's closed door.

script.say: No. She can't find out about the hospital. If she finds out the swap wasn't an accident, we both lose everything.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16; a phone on a tripod at the head of the table gives you a clean wide, then pick up close-ups handheld. Any home with a front door and a dining table works; dress the table with a cloth, candles and real food to sell the money. Light the dinner warm and soft, and the hallway cold with only a phone screen or one lamp. Record the whispered threat and the final call with the phone close to the actor's mouth. Film the pearl test in a tight close-up so the audience can see the clasp.

ul: Claire has two faces. In public every line is sugar; the whispers and the final call drop half an octave and lose the smile completely.
May wins by being calm. She never raises her voice, even when accused. The stiller she is, the harder the reversal hits.
Pause after Arthur lifts the necklace out of the bag. Let the whole table sit in that silence before Claire speaks.
Helen and Arthur must believe Claire at first. If they look suspicious too early, May's reveal loses its power.
Claire's tears should come too fast. A sharp viewer should notice; the others at the table should not.
Common mistake: playing May as angry. She is hurt, but she has handled liars at a market stall all her life.
Set the first meeting at the family's shop or restaurant instead of a house, with the missing item being the takings from the till.
Swap it to sons: the real son comes home and his brother hides a missing watch in his bag; May's skill with watches fits perfectly.
Change the cliffhanger so the person Claire calls is Helen's own sister, the aunt who was at the hospital on the night of the birth.

faq.q: Can I enter this script in a drama competition or film it for class?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0 for competitions, class projects and monetised channels alike. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the programme or the video description.

faq.q: Is the pearl test in the script real?
faq.a: It is a well-known rule of thumb that real pearls feel slightly gritty against a tooth while glass or plastic ones feel smooth. In the story it shows May's skill; for filming, any string of costume pearls will do.

faq.q: Can I make it with three actors?
faq.a: Yes. Merge Helen and Arthur into one parent and give the parent both sets of lines. The bag search and the final phone call still work exactly the same.
